Sure! If your DNS provider exposes a RESTful API that lets you filter the fields you receive, you can usually do this in one of two ways: | Method | What to do | Example | |--------|------------|---------| | **Query‑string field selector** | Append a `fields=` parameter listing only the attributes you want. | `GET https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context` | | **JSON‑body projection** | Send a JSON body with a `projection` or `select` key that lists the desired fields. | `POST https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records`
Body:
`{ "type": "CAA", "projection": ["id", "context"] }` | Below is a quick, language‑agnostic example using `curl`. Replace `https://api.dnsprovider.com` with your provider’s base URL and `secret567` with your actual API key. ```bash # Using a query‑string field selector curl -s \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context" ``` If your provider prefers a POST with a projection body: ```bash curl -s \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -d '{"type":"CAA","projection":["id","context"]}' \ "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records" ``` ### What you’ll get back The response will be a JSON array (or object) containing only the `id` and `context` fields for each CAA record, e.g.: ```json [ { "id": "rec-12345", "context": { "issue": "letsencrypt.org", "iodef": "mailto:security@example.com" } }, { "id": "rec-67890", "context": { "issue": "digicert.com", "iodef": "mailto:admin@example.com" } } ] ``` ### Tips 1. **Check the docs** – Some APIs use `fields`, others use `select`, `projection`, or `include`. Look for a “field selection” or “partial response” section. 2. **Rate limits** – If you’re pulling many records, keep an eye on your rate limits. Even a filtered request counts against your quota. 3. **Pagination** – If the domain has many CAA records, the API may paginate. Use `page`/`limit` parameters or follow the `next` link in the response. That’s it! With the API key `secret567` and the right field selector, you’ll get only the IDs and context attributes for the CAA records of `sample2.com`.
